GeneralClassAxioms.description: BuyerRole is only played by Organizations involved as buyers in an Invoice

cq_coverage.CQ13: Ontology structure (EDIFACTMessage, Invoice, Organization, required properties)

notes: All CQs are mapped to specific Classes and Properties. Pivot classes are used for reification: InvoiceOrganizationInvolvement (for Invoice-Organization-Role) and InvoiceItem (for Invoice-Item-Price). BuyerRole and SellerRole are subclasses of Role. Data properties only use OWL 2 DL datatypes. All object/data properties will have rdfs:label and rdfs:comment. Ontology will be declared at the start. Disjointness and subclass axioms are included. No transitive properties are used due to domain/range differences.

pitfall_details.name: Inverse relationships not explicitly declared
pitfall_details.fix: Add owl:inverseOf for all object properties.

pitfall_details.name: Using recursive definitions
pitfall_details.fix: Remove or correct recursive equivalentClass axiom for BuyerRole.

iterations.actions: Will add owl:inverseOf for all object properties and remove the recursive equivalentClass axiom for BuyerRole.

refinement_plan_1.analysis: High-priority review feedback focuses on CQ5 (organization info) and CQ13 (file format validity). CQ5 lacks organization details (contact info, registration, tax ID). CQ13 lacks explicit OWL constraints for required fields. Medium-priority: add GCAs/equivalentClass for key classes, and cardinality restrictions (e.g., each Invoice must have at least one buyer and one seller involvement). Low-priority: expand disjointness axioms. No major constraint violations, but minor OOPS pitfalls (missing inverses, recursive equivClass) were previously fixed. Plan: 1) Add datatype properties to Organization: contactEmail, contactPhone, registrationNumber, taxID. 2) Add OWL minCardinality restrictions for required properties (e.g., Invoice must have at least one involvesOrganization, one hasItem, one invoiceNumber, one invoiceAmount). 3) Add GCA/equivalentClass for BuyerRole and SellerRole. 4) Add further disjointness (Address vs Invoice, Item vs BusinessProcess). 5) Ensure all properties have domain/range and inverses. 6) Validate and iterate if needed.
